exempt.reason: No per-type hand-written encode/decode code: a property of generated code, not of bytes.
Single-expression entry points: a property of the public API's shape.
Free functions, not methods on the DTO: a property of the public API's shape.
Caller-supplied reusable output buffers: observable only as allocation behaviour, tested with a counting allocator.
Which libraries the runtime depends on is a property of its manifest, not of any byte sequence.
A MAY: a runtime may omit a range check the mapped type already makes redundant, so no input requires it.
The maximum nesting depth is configurable and the corpus format carries no configuration (D-010).
A MAY about pre-allocation clamping; the allocation is not observable from any input and output.
String and collection bounds are configurable and the corpus format carries no configuration (D-010).
no_std + alloc compatibility of the Rust runtime: a build property.
No exceptions and no RTTI in the C++ runtime: a compiler-flag build property.
No OS threading primitives in the core: a build property, enforced for Rust by the no_std build.
No filesystem or environment APIs in the core: a build property, enforced for Rust by the no_std build.
Exposing caller-supplied buffers and allocators where the primitive library allows: an API-shape property.
States what Lido does not guarantee (removal, rename, type change, key reuse, array insert, variant changes): there is no expected outcome to assert.
States that tables carry no added-field compatibility concern: there is nothing to assert.
